response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment/owner structure, transition-group guard collisions, wrong local-exit targets, unauthorized edges, and cross-context inconsistencies using exact source/model identities. Key findings: (1) NL2's InitialState->HighwayMode/UrbanMode alternatives share a common owner (AutonomousMode) and the FCSTM realizes them with exact matching guards (high_way_true/urban_way_true), so endpoints and guard-disjointness are satisfied and omitted. (2) NL3/NL5's enter_hwy/cruise alternatives are realized in the closed model with two distinct triggers (dist_to_front_25 vs dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true), so guard_disjointness is satisfied at the model level and omitted. (3) NL4/NL5 cruise<->lane_change bidirectional endpoints are present and correct, omitted. (4) NL6/NL10 termination targets FinishState which is nested inside HighwayMode; UrbanMode's termination edges (tr_0021/tr_0023) target AutonomousMode.HighwayMode.FinishState per the exact source inventory, and the closed model realizes the full path through route tokens, so the target concept resolves uniquely though I omit an exact model_element_ref since the direct closed-model edge is a composite-to-composite jump routed through R45RouteToken rather than a single directly-named edge; I treat this as informational and do not force an invalid exact semantic binding. (5) The CollisionAvoidance subsystem owns required NL12/NL13 activation/deactivation behavior via its own local initial edge (CollisionAvoidance->collision_avoidance_deactive, transition:line:86), but the composite itself is never entered from root or AutonomousMode anywhere in the complete source or closed-model transition inventory. Deterministic diagnostics (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL) and verify_facts (reachability refuted for CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active; event-consumer checks refuted for both CollisionAvoidance events) confirm this. This is the canonical case of an owning composite lacking exact default entry from root, justifying one derived reachability contract distinct from the already-satisfied local initial-entry edge (which correctly targets collision_avoidance_deactive within its own owner scope). I also raise a supporting event-consumer-coverage-style observation on the initial_entry contract itself (predicate-null W1) because the practical operational obligation stated by NL12 ('is initially in') can never be realized given the composite's total isolation, while carefully not converting the already structurally-valid local initial pseudostate edge into a false violation of its own narrow property.

output.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment/owner structure, transition-group guard collisions, wrong local-exit targets, unauthorized edges, and cross-context inconsistencies using exact source/model identities. Key findings: (1) NL2's InitialState->HighwayMode/UrbanMode alternatives share a common owner (AutonomousMode) and the FCSTM realizes them with exact matching guards (high_way_true/urban_way_true), so endpoints and guard-disjointness are satisfied and omitted. (2) NL3/NL5's enter_hwy/cruise alternatives are realized in the closed model with two distinct triggers (dist_to_front_25 vs dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true), so guard_disjointness is satisfied at the model level and omitted. (3) NL4/NL5 cruise<->lane_change bidirectional endpoints are present and correct, omitted. (4) NL6/NL10 termination targets FinishState which is nested inside HighwayMode; UrbanMode's termination edges (tr_0021/tr_0023) target AutonomousMode.HighwayMode.FinishState per the exact source inventory, and the closed model realizes the full path through route tokens, so the target concept resolves uniquely though I omit an exact model_element_ref since the direct closed-model edge is a composite-to-composite jump routed through R45RouteToken rather than a single directly-named edge; I treat this as informational and do not force an invalid exact semantic binding. (5) The CollisionAvoidance subsystem owns required NL12/NL13 activation/deactivation behavior via its own local initial edge (CollisionAvoidance->collision_avoidance_deactive, transition:line:86), but the composite itself is never entered from root or AutonomousMode anywhere in the complete source or closed-model transition inventory. Deterministic diagnostics (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL) and verify_facts (reachability refuted for CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active; event-consumer checks refuted for both CollisionAvoidance events) confirm this. This is the canonical case of an owning composite lacking exact default entry from root, justifying one derived reachability contract distinct from the already-satisfied local initial-entry edge (which correctly targets collision_avoidance_deactive within its own owner scope). I also raise a supporting event-consumer-coverage-style observation on the initial_entry contract itself (predicate-null W1) because the practical operational obligation stated by NL12 ('is initially in') can never be realized given the composite's total isolation, while carefully not converting the already structurally-valid local initial pseudostate edge into a false violation of its own narrow property.

Since the model provides two distinct triggers, guard_disjointness contract is satisfied by the closed model despite the NL prose's apparent overlap; NL3-GUARD-1 is satisfied and omitted. (3) NL4/NL5 cruise<->lane_change bidirectional endpoints are present and correct. (4) NL6/NL10 termination targets FinishState which is nested inside HighwayMode (AutonomousMode.HighwayMode.FinishState) rather than at AutonomousMode scope directly - UrbanMode's termination edge (tr_0021/tr_0023, transition:line:56/58) actually targets HighwayMode.FinishState (cross-composite jump), which is unusual structurally but exists in the model. (7) NL11's dynamic HighwayMode<->UrbanMode transitions are realized only indirectly via R45RouteToken routing (tr_0024/tr_0025 in source inventory become transition:line:73/74 in FCSTM with guard R45RouteToken==24/25, not directly by urban_way_true/high_way_true events) -- but exact endpoints (HighwayMode->UrbanMode and UrbanMode->HighwayMode) do exist in the complete transition inventory, so NL11-ENDPOINT-1/2 are structurally satisfied; the guard realization difference is a guard-fact concern, not endpoint existence, and no explicit guard contract was extracted for NL11, so omitted from structural analysis. arguments.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, containment/owner structure, transition-group guard collisions, wrong local-exit targets, unauthorized edges, and cross-context inconsistencies using exact source/model identities. Key findings: (1) NL2's InitialState->HighwayMode/UrbanMode alternatives share a common owner (AutonomousMode) and the FCSTM realizes them with exact matching guards (high_way_true/urban_way_true), so endpoints and guard-disjointness are satisfied and omitted. (2) NL3/NL5's enter_hwy/cruise alternatives are realized in the closed model with two distinct triggers (dist_to_front_25 vs dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true), so guard_disjointness is satisfied at the model level and omitted. (3) NL4/NL5 cruise<->lane_change bidirectional endpoints are present and correct, omitted. (4) NL6/NL10 termination targets FinishState which is nested inside HighwayMode; UrbanMode's termination edges (tr_0021/tr_0023) target AutonomousMode.HighwayMode.FinishState per the exact source inventory, and the closed model realizes the full path through route tokens, so the target concept resolves uniquely though I omit an exact model_element_ref since the direct closed-model edge is a composite-to-composite jump routed through R45RouteToken rather than a single directly-named edge; I treat this as informational and do not force an invalid exact semantic binding. (5) The CollisionAvoidance subsystem owns required NL12/NL13 activation/deactivation behavior via its own local initial edge (CollisionAvoidance->collision_avoidance_deactive, transition:line:86), but the composite itself is never entered from root or AutonomousMode anywhere in the complete source or closed-model transition inventory. Deterministic diagnostics (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL) and verify_facts (reachability refuted for CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active; event-consumer checks refuted for both CollisionAvoidance events) confirm this. This is the canonical case of an owning composite lacking exact default entry from root, justifying one derived reachability contract distinct from the already-satisfied local initial-entry edge (which correctly targets collision_avoidance_deactive within its own owner scope). I also raise a supporting event-consumer-coverage-style observation on the initial_entry contract itself (predicate-null W1) because the practical operational obligation stated by NL12 ('is initially in') can never be realized given the composite's total isolation, while carefully not converting the already structurally-valid local initial pseudostate edge into a false violation of its own narrow property.

response.reason: This lens audits root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, termination stability, and dead-end/frontier facts using the closed FCSTM's inspection-equivalent, verify, and SMT facts. (2) Both event-consumer contracts on the collision avoidance events (pedestrian_detected... and front_inactive...) have declared consumers but zero reachable consumers per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers and verify_facts non_proved rows -- this directly violates the derived NL12 event_consumer_coverage supplied contract's operational-coverage requirement; NL13 lacks a corresponding event_consumer_coverage contract in the NL-only extraction, so I derive one for the deactivation event under NL13's namespace. (3) NL6/NL10 termination contracts to FinishState: FinishState is reachable but has exact outgoing transitions rerouting into continued operation (urban_way_true, auto_finished_true effects on R45RouteToken) rather than closing to a stable terminal -- this supports a termination candidate for both NL6-TERM-1 and NL10-TERM-1. (4) The straight-state progress/deadlock contract (NL7-DERIVED) is satisfied: straight has multiple reachable outgoing transitions, so no deadlock issue is emitted for it. (5) All core mode-shift, endpoint, and guard contracts for HighwayMode/UrbanMode/enter_hwy/etc. are structurally satisfied per inspection-equivalent inventory and are omitted as sparse output.

result.reason: This lens audits root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, termination stability, and dead-end/frontier facts using the closed FCSTM's inspection-equivalent, verify, and SMT facts. Key findings: (1) CollisionAvoidance and its two states are entirely unreachable from root (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / verify refuted), so NL12's initial_entry contract for collision_avoidance_deactive is satisfied locally by transition:line:86 but the owning composite itself is unreachable -- a distinct reachability gap not covered by any supplied contract, so I derive one against the owning composite. (2) Both event-consumer contracts on the collision avoidance events (pedestrian_detected... and front_inactive...) have declared consumers but zero reachable consumers per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers and verify_facts non_proved rows -- this directly violates the derived NL12 event_consumer_coverage supplied contract's operational-coverage requirement; NL13 lacks a corresponding event_consumer_coverage contract in the NL-only extraction, so I derive one for the deactivation event under NL13's namespace. (3) NL6/NL10 termination contracts to FinishState: FinishState is reachable but has exact outgoing transitions rerouting into continued operation (urban_way_true, auto_finished_true effects on R45RouteToken) rather than closing to a stable terminal -- this supports a termination candidate for both NL6-TERM-1 and NL10-TERM-1. (4) The straight-state progress/deadlock contract (NL7-DERIVED) is satisfied: straight has multiple reachable outgoing transitions, so no deadlock issue is emitted for it. (5) All core mode-shift, endpoint, and guard contracts for HighwayMode/UrbanMode/enter_hwy/etc. are structurally satisfied per inspection-equivalent inventory and are omitted as sparse output.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for the pedestrian_detected composite event; verify_facts.non_proved check on transition:line:87; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE.
decisions.reason: The event-consumer coverage contract requires the pedestrian_detected activation event to have a reachable consumer within collision_avoidance_deactive; inspection_equivalent_facts shows the declared consumer transition:line:87 but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] and verify_facts refutes the check, establishing the violation. A declared consumer does not rebut the reachable-consumer requirement per the property-preserving protocol, so the upstream-attribution reading survives only as a non-dispositive undercutting alternative, not a rebuttal.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The consumer transition and its source state exist exactly as authored and are declaratively correct; a competent alternative reading attributes the unreachability entirely to the upstream initial-entry/reachability defect in the enclosing CollisionAvoidance composite rather than to a defect intrinsic to the event-consumption relation itself.
decisions.violated_obligation: The activation event/condition must be consumable (reachable) within the collision_avoidance_deactive operating scope to trigger activation during actual system execution.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for the deactivation composite event; verify_facts.non_proved check on transition:line:88; NL13 quote.
decisions.reason: NL13 requires the deactivation event (front_inactive/rear_inactive/pedestrian_inactive) to be consumable within collision_avoidance_active; inspection_equivalent_facts shows the declared consumer transition:line:88 but empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs, and verify_facts refutes the check, establishing the violation. A declared consumer does not rebut the reachable-consumer requirement, so the upstream-attribution alternative survives only as a non-dispositive undercutting reading.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The deactivation transition exists exactly as authored with the correct guard/effect semantics; a competent alternative reading attributes the unreachability entirely to the separate CollisionAvoidance-composite reachability gap rather than to a flaw in the deactivation relation itself.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states row for CollisionAvoidance; verify_facts.non_proved reachability check; NL12 quote.
decisions.reason: NL12/NL13 establish CollisionAvoidance as a required operating subsystem whose activation/deactivation behavior must execute; inspection_equivalent_facts shows reachable_from_initial=false with empty outgoing_transition_refs and verify_facts refutes reachability, and no transition in the closed model targets CollisionAvoidance from root or AutonomousMode, establishing the violation. The orthogonal-region rebuttal is not supported by any exact NL terminal/parallel-region clause or explicit supplied fact designating CollisionAvoidance as an independent region; absent such exact support, this alleged rebuttal is defeated by the exact supplied model facts showing it as a plain sibling composite with no declared parallel-region semantics.
decisions.strongest_defeater: CollisionAvoidance may be intentionally modeled as an independently-initialized parallel top-level region under orthogonal-region UML semantics, so its own initial pseudostate edge suffices for entry and the 'unreachable from root' finding is a diagnostic artifact of the finite-hierarchy reachability algorithm rather than a genuine authoring defect.
decisions.violated_obligation: The CollisionAvoidance operating composite must be reachable from root/system so the activation/deactivation behavior it hosts can execute.

decisions.basis: NL6/NL10 quotes; source_contract continuation_ids tr_0024/tr_0029; PlantUML lines 33 and 43; element_refs for HighwayMode, UrbanMode, FinishState, transition:line:73.
decisions.reason: NL6 and NL10 both require HighwayMode and UrbanMode to end by transitioning to FinishState as a completion boundary; the exact source facts show FinishState is not explicit-final and its ancestor chain admits guard-free continuations (tr_0024, tr_0029), so the shared target does not provide a stable termination boundary, establishing the violation per the property-preserving protocol (an existing endpoint does not by itself rebut failed stable termination). The proposed rebuttal that endpoint existence alone satisfies the termination clause is exactly the kind of weaker-property substitution the protocol excludes, so it is defeated by the exact non-final/continuation facts.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The existence of each completion endpoint transition into FinishState might be argued to already satisfy NL6/NL10's termination clauses regardless of FinishState's own outgoing continuations.
decisions.violated_obligation: The completion obligations for HighwayMode and UrbanMode must reach shared target FinishState as a stable termination boundary.

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states row for FinishState (line:21) shows outgoing_transition_refs=[transition:line:36, transition:line:40], both reachable_from_initial=true; fcstm_model.text lines for 'FinishState -> [*] : /urban_way_true' and 'FinishState -> [*] : /auto_finished_true'; NL6 contract quote establishing HighwayMode completion via FinishState.

issues.observed: The closed FCSTM shows FinishState (line:21) with outgoing transitions FinishState -> [*] on urban_way_true (effect R45RouteToken=24) and FinishState -> [*] on auto_finished_true (effect R45RouteToken=29), which exit HighwayMode's local scope and, via the enclosing AutonomousMode-level routed transitions (UrbanMode->HighwayMode on R45RouteToken==24, and HighwayMode-> [*] on R45RouteToken==29 exiting AutonomousMode entirely or looping via AutonomousMode->AutonomousMode self-transition on R45RouteToken==29), permit re-entry into HighwayMode/UrbanMode operation or an ambiguous root-level self-loop rather than closing to a stable terminal state.
issues.reason: Per the termination-audit discipline, every termination_state contract requires inspecting the exact target and all active-ancestor continuations; a present edge into FinishState does not rebut instability if the ancestor state can further transition. The FinishState state has exact non-empty outgoing transitions (line:36, line:40) reachable_from_initial=true, so the completion state is not a dead sink and can continue routing.

semantic_adjudication.reason: NL12/NL13 describe activation/deactivation behavior owned by CollisionAvoidance as part of the same system description, implying it must actually execute during runs of the described system; exact_source_inventory and fcstm_model show no transition anywhere enters CollisionAvoidance from root or AutonomousMode, and inspection_equivalent_facts/verify_facts confirm reachable_from_initial=false and refuted reachability for CollisionAvoidance and its children. The orthogonal-region rebuttal is not supported by any exact NL clause or formal fact establishing CollisionAvoidance as an independently-initialized parallel region; the NL narrative ties its behavior into the single autonomous-driving system description, so the alleged rebuttal is defeated by the exact supplied continuation/operational contract.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: CollisionAvoidance could be an intentionally independent top-level region whose own local initial edge suffices for entry under orthogonal-region UML semantics, making root-level entry unnecessary and the reachability finding a diagnostic artifact rather than an authoring defect.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: CollisionAvoidance, as the owner of required activation/deactivation behavior, must be reachable from the model root so that behavior can execute during any system run.

response.reason: The primary plan thoroughly covers containment, initial entry, endpoints, terminations, and aggregate guard_disjointness/guard contracts for every numbered segment. However, several independently violable obligations remain unextracted: (1) NL2's two branch guards (high_way=true, urban_way=true) are exact per-alternative conditions distinguishable from the aggregate guard_disjointness contract already present, and a mismatch on one exact guard is independently testable; (2) NL6 and NL10 each name an exact triggering condition (auto_finished=true) for mode termination that constitutes an event-consumer coverage obligation distinct from the termination endpoint contract; (3) NL12 names pedestrian_detected as one specific activation-causing indicator among a disjunction, which is an independently violable event-consumer obligation separate from the bundled guard contract; (4) NL9's explicit onward-continuation requirement for the straight state establishes a deadlock-freedom/progress obligation not present in the primary plan. No other segment yields an additional independently violable obligation; cardinality, region-structure, and remaining transition/guard/action clauses are already represented by the primary plan's typed contracts and transition groups.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for pedestrian_detected event; verify_facts.non_proved event-consumer check; element_refs transition:line:87 and state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:84.
decisions.reason: NL12 requires the pedestrian_detected activation transition to be reachable and consumable; inspection_equivalent_facts shows the declared consumer transition:line:87 exists with the correct trigger but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty, and verify_facts refutes the event-consumer check, establishing the candidate's semantic obligation. The competent alternative reading is that this is purely a downstream symptom of the separate CollisionAvoidance composite-root unreachability rather than a distinct local defect; because both the local consumer-coverage framing and the upstream reachability framing are compatible with the same exact facts, this alternative reading survives as an undercutting defeater rather than being defeated outright.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The activation transition exists exactly as specified with the correct disjunctive guard, so an alternative reading attributes the entire defect to the separate, already-identified root-unreachability of the owning CollisionAvoidance composite rather than to a missing or malformed local consumer edge.
decisions.violated_obligation: The pedestrian_detected-driven activation transition (collision_avoidance_deactive -> collision_avoidance_active) must be reachable and its event consumable during operation.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states row for collision_avoidance_deactive reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts.non_proved reachability check; fcstm_model text showing no root-to-CollisionAvoidance transition.
decisions.reason: NL12 states the collision avoidance system 'is initially in' collision_avoidance_deactive as an operational fact. The exact local initial edge (transition:line:86) exists and targets the correct state, but inspection_equivalent_facts marks the state reachable_from_initial=false and verify_facts refutes reachability, because the enclosing CollisionAvoidance has no incoming edge from root. This establishes a genuine operational gap in the candidate's obligation, while the exact local initial-entry syntax being well-formed supports a competent alternative reading that the owner-local contract is separately satisfied and the defect belongs to the reachability contract; both readings remain compatible with the same facts, so the alternative survives as an undercutting defeater.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The owner-local initial pseudostate edge CollisionAvoidance -> collision_avoidance_deactive is syntactically well-formed and correctly targets the state, so a competent reading treats this owner-local initial_entry contract as satisfied and attributes the practical unreachability defect exclusively to the separate derived reachability contract on CollisionAvoidance.
decisions.violated_obligation: collision_avoidance_deactive must be the reachable initial operating state of the collision avoidance subsystem during system execution.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states row for CollisionAvoidance; verify_facts.non_proved reachability check; fcstm_model.text; NL12/NL13 quotes.
decisions.reason: NL12/NL13 describe activation/deactivation behavior owned by CollisionAvoidance as part of the same system description, implying it must actually execute during runs of the described system; exact_source_inventory and fcstm_model show no transition anywhere enters CollisionAvoidance from root or AutonomousMode, and inspection_equivalent_facts/verify_facts confirm reachable_from_initial=false and refuted reachability for CollisionAvoidance and its children. The orthogonal-region rebuttal is not supported by any exact NL clause or formal fact establishing CollisionAvoidance as an independently-initialized parallel region; the NL narrative ties its behavior into the single autonomous-driving system description, so the alleged rebuttal is defeated by the exact supplied continuation/operational contract.
decisions.strongest_defeater: CollisionAvoidance could be an intentionally independent top-level region whose own local initial edge suffices for entry under orthogonal-region UML semantics, making root-level entry unnecessary and the reachability finding a diagnostic artifact rather than an authoring defect.
decisions.violated_obligation: CollisionAvoidance, as the owner of required activation/deactivation behavior, must be reachable from the model root so that behavior can execute during any system run.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for the pedestrian_detected composite event; verify_facts.non_proved check on transition:line:87; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE.

(4) The straight-state progress/deadlock contract (NL7-DERIVED) is satisfied: straight has multiple reachable outgoing transitions, so no deadlock issue is emitted for it. (5) All core mode-shift, endpoint, and guard contracts for HighwayMode/UrbanMode/enter_hwy/etc. are structurally satisfied per inspection-equivalent inventory and are omitted as sparse output.
